title: Microsoft Purview: permanently delete OneDrive and SharePoint files with Priority cleanup (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: the government-cloud roadmap facts, deletion safeguards, licensing and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections would complete the wizard route, distinguish portal and PowerShell audit permissions, and identify checklist controls missing from the table.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The roadmap describes 93 days in ODSP Recycle Bins as protection against inadvertent data loss.
claims.quote: To help prevent inadvertent data loss, M365 retention labels policies and M365 retention policies do not hard delete content immediately and keeps the data in Recycle Bins for 93 days for ODSP.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes hard delete as costly because data loss from policy misconfiguration or regression has legal implications.
claims.quote: Hard delete itself is a very costly process as it opens Microsoft to heavy legal implications in case of any data loss incident that may occur due to a misconfigured policy or regression.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes bypassing retention and eDiscovery holds for changing legal requirements or data spillage.
claims.quote: Priority Cleanup feature allows users to bypass retention, and eDiscovery holds to help customers comply to changing legal/compliance requirements or manage data spillage scenarios.

claims.claim: These permanently deleted files cannot be recovered from the Recycle Bins.
claims.quote: Deleted content bypasses the recycle bins and isn't recoverable under ordinary circumstances.

claims.claim: The roadmap description does not say that existing behaviour changes automatically on arrival.
claims.quote: Ability to select hard delete configuration for a Priority cleanup policy for OneDrive and SharePoint content and skip recycle bins.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup itself is enabled by default at tenant level.
claims.quote: Because of the built-in safeguards, the feature itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.

claims.claim: The tenant switch is at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup settings > Configuration > control for priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management. From the top right, select Priority cleanup settings. From the Configuration page, turn off the control for priority cleanup, and select Save.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API or PowerShell call for the tenant-wide Priority cleanup switch.
claims.quote: Searched: priority cleanup tenant enable disable PowerShell PriorityCleanupEnabled permanent deletion New-RetentionCompliancePolicy parameter; "priority cleanup" "Set-" tenant configuration enable disable. Read the workload settings instructions and returned PowerShell references; no tenant-switch call.

claims.quote: When you turn off priority cleanup, you're turning it off for Exchange as well as for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Turning off the tenant switch prevents new Priority cleanup policies being created.
claims.quote: New priority cleanup policies can't be created until you turn on the control and select Save again.

claims.claim: Existing policies continue to function when the tenant switch is off.
claims.quote: If priority cleanup policies are already created when you turn off the control: Existing priority cleanup policies continue to function

claims.quote: Existing priority cleanup policies can be deleted

claims.claim: Existing policies cannot be modified when the tenant switch is off.
claims.quote: Existing priority cleanup policies can't be modified

claims.quote: The Priority Cleanup Viewer role allows only the visibility of priority cleanup policies and settings without the ability to make changes or create new policies.

claims.claim: No documented automation selects the permanent-deletion option, and New-RetentionCompliancePolicy does not describe how to select it.

Read New-RetentionCompliancePolicy and New-RetentionComplianceRule in full, returned Set references and permanent-deletion guidance; no documented switch or property selects permanent file deletion.

Add the omitted query-entry page: 'Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > + Create a priority cleanup > Choose the type of priority cleanup > Static > Policy for SharePoint/OneDrive > Tell us what you're looking for > Choose what to do with the content > Delete data permanently'.

claims.claim: The audit search page is at Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search.

claims.fix: Replace the final sentence of controls[3].note with 'Needs the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role in the Microsoft Purview portal for UI search, or in the Exchange admin center for PowerShell.'

claims.claim: The permanent-deletion page gives no completion interval after final approval.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" "days" approval completion timing. Read priority-cleanup-permanent-deletion in full and the standard workflow approval section; the permanent-deletion page gives no approval-to-completion interval.

claims.claim: The standard workflow page says to allow up to seven days for deletion.
claims.quote: Items that are approved or relabeled are then moved to the Disposed items tab. Allow up to seven days for items to be deleted.

claims.claim: Approvers review identified items on the Pending cleanups page.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, go to Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > Pending cleanups. Select the cleanup and review the identified items, their locations, and their history.

claims.where: Governance guidance; Governance controls: prerequisite note
claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to check or configure controls that have no corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Review membership of the Organization Management role group ... Turn on auditing ... Assign approver roles ... Run simulation ... The Before rollout checks ... are prerequisite checks, and the table does not give routes for configuring them.
claims.fix: The Before rollout steps reviewing Organization Management membership, enabling auditing and assigning approver roles, and the At rollout simulation/review step have no matching control row. Calling them prerequisites does not exempt them from the checklist/table rule. Record this coverage gap; do not add rows in this correction.
